# URLCode audit

> Operator-installed audit log: other extensions record privileged actions
> into one bounded SQLite file (data/audit.sqlite) through a transactional
> outbox they own, and readers query it. Serves no routes. Released with core
> and installed with `urlcode extensions add audit` (auth requires it).
> Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.audit: { version: "1", config: { retention: 100000 } }`;
  `retention` is 1000..10000000 and is the only setting.
- No routes: a route with `extension: audit` is refused at startup.
- Which actions are audited belongs to the producers: auth always, and a store
  collection with `audit: true`.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): the exports, the event bounds, the query, the producer
  contract and the CLI.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md): the delivery guarantee, retention and storage.

## Do not guess
- Do not write audit rows from a handler or a hook; declare the producing
  feature (for example a store collection's `audit: true`) instead.
- Audit enforces no permission. Readers check `audit.read` and `audit.export`
  (granted to roles in the auth operator module).
- Node only (`node:sqlite`); other targets are refused before serving.
- `urlcode-audit list` takes `{"database": "<absolute path>", "query": {...}}`
  on stdin and prints one page of at most 100 events.
